misconception_description: Student believes that values must be explicitly converted to their current type to ensure type safety.

solutions.generated_code:
program CekTandaBerlawanan
kamus
  a, b : integer
  hasil : boolean
algoritma
  input(a, b)
  a <- integer(a)
  b <- integer(b)
  if (integer(a) < 0 and integer(b) > 0) or (integer(a) > 0 and integer(b) < 0) then
    hasil <- boolean(true)
  else
    hasil <- boolean(false)
  endif
  output(boolean(hasil))
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student explicitly converts x and y to int type even though they are already expected to be integers, and converts the boolean result to bool type even though comparison operators already return booleans. The student believes these conversions are necessary for type safety and proper code structure. The code functions correctly but includes unnecessary type conversions. This reflects the student's belief that explicit type conversion ensures type safety even when the values are already of the correct type.
